requirements.title: Calculate core process-time metrics
requirements.user: Lean Six Sigma practitioner or analyst
requirements.need: Calculate lead time, wait time, process-cycle efficiency, and takt time from observed process data without rebuilding the formulas for each project.
requirements.acceptance: The public API accepts explicit metric inputs, returns documented values in requested units, and rejects negative or impossible durations and non-positive demand.
requirements.evidence: 2026-10-24 acceptance audit: current timing calculations work on governed valid inputs, but wait_time has no unit declaration and always labels hours; negative and nonfinite inputs can return results. See tools/audit_v02_readiness.py and docs/assessments/v02-release-readiness.md.

requirements.title: Calculate stage and rolled yield
requirements.need: Measure created-to-booked, booked-to-completed, and combined conversion yield from observed binary stage outcomes.
requirements.acceptance: Each stage yield uses its eligible prior-stage population, rolled yield combines configured stages, and invalid binary values or impossible stage progression produce clear errors.
requirements.evidence: README.md; src/lss4py/yellow_belt.py; tests/test_yellow_belt.py

requirements.title: Combine an explicit process model with observed event data
requirements.user: Analyst working with a FLO-derived or programmatically created process model
requirements.need: Calculate metrics using both declared process structure and observed data, including parallel work and rework.
requirements.acceptance: Metric bindings can come from ProcessModelIR; explicit call arguments take precedence; parallel timing supports critical-path and sum-all-branches semantics; unmodeled overlap, unknown steps, and unmodeled repetition are rejected.
requirements.evidence: README.md contract; src/lss4py/domain/models.py; tests/test_yellow_belt.py

requirements.title: Understand assumptions and invalid inputs
requirements.user: Any practitioner relying on an analysis for an improvement decision
requirements.need: Receive explicit validation failures, assumptions, and warnings instead of plausible-looking results from invalid data or unmet statistical assumptions.
requirements.acceptance: Stable public metric and yield APIs fail invalid structural inputs with an LSS4PY exception, and validate_event_log returns machine-readable warnings for inspectable event-log issues.
requirements.evidence: 2026-10-24 acceptance audit reproduces accepted negative wait inputs and nonfinite wait/PCE/takt observations. Structured preparation and book contracts reject these domains, but older default timing paths do not yet meet the complete invalid-input criterion; tools/audit_v02_readiness.py; docs/assessments/v02-release-readiness.md

requirements.title: Reproduce R SixSigma analytical results
requirements.user: Python practitioner migrating a workflow or curriculum from R SixSigma
requirements.need: Obtain equivalent numerical results and analytical artifacts through idiomatic Python workflows for the retained R SixSigma surface.
requirements.acceptance: Each claimed compatibility feature has a mapped user outcome, versioned R fixture where numerical, documented tolerance, and an explicit note for intentional differences.
requirements.evidence: Actual SixSigma 0.11.1 Cp/Cpk/Z/yield baselines are generated and verified; Cp/Cpk/Z and defect/rework yield have passing Python tests; remaining retained R methods are incomplete; docs/sixsigma-compatibility.md; docs/reference-fixtures.md

requirements.title: Use any supported dataframe backend
requirements.user: Analyst whose data is already in pandas, Polars, or PyArrow
requirements.need: Run the same supported analysis without manually converting the entire input to the dataframe library chosen by LSS4PY.
requirements.acceptance: Pandas and Polars inputs pass equivalent contract tests; PyArrow tables work where supported; backend-specific exceptions and any copy/materialization are documented; no pandas index is required.
requirements.evidence: Polars is canonical ingestion; shared pandas/Polars contracts cover all current tabular calculations and non-default indexes; Arrow is tested case-by-case with a documented timestamp-string limitation; broader null/coercion contracts remain open; docs/backend-contracts.md; tests/test_backend_contracts.py

requirements.title: Validate and normalize analytical data
requirements.need: Inspect schema, keys, timestamps, units, missingness, duplicates, and invalid domains before trusting a result.
requirements.acceptance: A reusable validation result identifies blocking errors and non-blocking warnings without mutating the source; normalization choices are explicit and reproducible.
requirements.evidence: Explicit DataContract inspection and opt-in canonical normalization cover schema, keys, timestamps, units, missingness, duplicates and numeric domains without source mutation; reports retain blocking/warning findings and original row positions; docs/data-quality.md; tests/test_data_quality.py; tests/test_data_contract.py; e2e/test_data_quality.py

requirements.acceptance: Guidance explains why methods are candidates, never silently executes a test from observed data alone, and records the method the user chooses.

requirements.title: Evaluate a fixed customer promise on an explicit cohort
requirements.need: See promise eligibility, misses, and miss rate without confusing readiness deadlines with lead-time allowances or ineligible orders with on-time orders.
requirements.acceptance: Eligibility is arrival <= 120 operating minutes and a miss is eligible readiness > 600; readiness exactly 600 is on time. Return eligible count, miss count, and rate with ineligible orders kept distinct. Friday 91 reproduces 6 misses / 21 eligible orders = 28.6%.
requirements.evidence: Public deadline_performance returns fixed-deadline misses/count/rate and eligible/on-time/ineligible case evidence; equality, undefined denominator, missing/invalid inputs and pinned 6/21 fixture pass supported backend tests; tests/test_prepared_preview.py; docs/book-preview.md

requirements.title: Calculate cohort efficiency with a consistent denominator
requirements.need: Compare summed value-added processing with summed operating lead time for the same explicitly selected orders.
requirements.acceptance: Cohort PCE is 100 * sum(order VA) / sum(order operating lead time), rather than the unweighted mean of order percentages. Use the book order-level right-first-time Wash, Dry, Fold and package, and Send readiness notification processing convention; exclude failed packaging attempts, corrections, staging (RNVA), intake, sorting, setup, and waiting from VA, preserve RNVA/NVA distinctions, and do not call every non-VA minute avoidable waste. Friday 91 reproduces 3535.3 / 25840.5 minutes = 13.7%.
requirements.evidence: Public process_cycle_efficiency aggregation=cohort returns a ratio of aligned VA/lead sums with explicit keys/count/unit/clock/boundary/VA convention and denominator evidence; pinned fixture gives 13.7%; tests/test_prepared_preview.py; examples/white_belt/preview-bundle.json
